A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VHD/VHR research. All 13 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination evaluations, VHD distribution analyses, ablations, timing measurements, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds outlier-removal ablations and expanded language-quality evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same VHD/T-VHD calculations, outlier filtering, sample-specific head selection, and reinforcement procedure. The new outlier ablation tests the component already defined in v1 Equation 6.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CHAIR on COCO, POPE with random/popular/adversarial splits, and LLaVA-Bench (In-the-Wild). Adding InstructBLIP results and naturalness scoring does not introduce different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Greedy, Beam, DoLa, VCD, OPERA, CODE, and the same Zhang et al. method, renamed from EHA to EAH. Table 3 extends the existing unmodified-model versus VHR comparison to another backbone.

E3.justification: LLaVA-Bench adds InstructBLIP evaluation, changes the judge from GPT-4o-mini to GPT-4o, and introduces naturalness scoring (Table 3; Appendix G). Section 4.4 changes the reported InstructBLIP reinforcement setting from the second plus last 18 layers to only the last 18 layers. Benchmark splits and generation limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds an outlier-removal ablation across all three backbones, testing whether the existing filtering rule helps head selection. The fixed-head comparison, layer and scale-factor analyses, timing comparison, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v3 removes v1's statements that GPT judging was repeated four times, averaged, and conducted with swapped response order (Table 3; Appendix G). The later repetition count is unspecified; this does not establish that repetitions stopped. CHAIR retains five-seed means and standard deviations.

E6.justification: Several VHR results change: InstructBLIP CHAIR scores become 37.76/9.75 instead of 38.68/10.09 alongside its revised layer setting; LLaVA-1.5 POPE F1 changes from 85.54 to 85.47. Table 3 replaces scores under the changed judge and adds InstructBLIP/naturalness entries. Table 4 adds outlier results, while most existing results and overall trends remain stable.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Proposition 1, and Appendix B proof are retained without substantive changes. Minor notation and wording corrections do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: VHD probes visual sensitivity, language bias relates to hallucination, and training-free VHR improves hallucination performance with negligible additional time.

C2.justification: v3 adds a limitation about ineffective or unstable second-layer reinforcement (Appendix C), discusses POPE's binary-task limitation, and interprets naturalness results. Its new claim that outlier removal consistently helps is not supported by the LLaVA-NeXT rows: outlier VHR scores 24.64/6.37 versus VHR's 24.96/6.80, with lower values better.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability link, specifies InstructBLIP's 7B size, clarifies that Len counts words, and supplies the expanded naturalness judging prompt. The PDFs do not establish whether the linked code is accessible or complete.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations on language bias and model interpretability, including Ghosh et al., Parcalabescu and Frank, and Zhou/Fang/He works. It replaces the EFUF alignment citation with RLHF-V and expands related-work discussion while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the analysis explanation, related work, conclusion, and Appendices A and G. Headings, terminology, affiliations, and acknowledgements are updated, while the main section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 4 gain columns or rows, Table 4 gains separate model/method columns, and Table 7's prompt expands. Captions and labels are refined, and appendix figures are rearranged. All ten figures and the two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The added outlier ablation and naturalness assessment make the intervention's effects easier to evaluate, while the code link and second-layer caveat improve documentation. These provide a modest overall gain. The gain is limited by lost GPT repetition/order-swap disclosure and an overgeneralized outlier-removal interpretation that Table 4 does not uniformly support.
